facts.text: Elkton was founded in 1886 when pioneer McGillivray built the first house and named the town after an elk he killed on his wife’s clothesline.
The village grew around the Saginaw, Tuscola & Huron Railroad, which linked Thumb farms to city markets and made Elkton a key depot for the Pere Marquette line.
By 1907 Elkton boasted a full 12‑grade school, a public library, and a bustling grain elevator that stored wheat and corn for farmers along the tracks.
The historic Elkton Hotel, a three‑story brick landmark, once stood at the north end of town and was a social hub for early residents.
Every month the Elkton Area Historical Society meets at the Heritage Center to preserve and share the village’s unique past with locals and visitors alike.
